symptom: An enumeration split `case $S/C when … end case` that left an enumeration value without a branch (CE0079), named a value the enumeration does not have, or the right value in another case (CE1613), or named a value in two branches (CE0771) passed `check` and `exec`; the build rejected each. Only the missing `(empty)` branch (MDL056) and an `else` were refused.
file: mdl/executor/validate_enum_split_values.go: checkEnumSplitDuplicateValues (MDL105, microflow and nanoflow validators) and enumSplitValueViolations (MDL106, called from TypeCheckProgram next to the expression hints). Tests: validate_enum_split_values_test.go; fixtures mdl-examples/bug-tests/enum-split-duplicate-values.fail.mdl and enum-split-values.mdl
cause: MDL056 was written knowing the other half of CE0079, a value with no branch, 'needs the enumeration's member list' and was left undone (its own comment says so); the member list is exactly what the catalog-backed tier already holds (exprcatalog.Reader.EnumCases / AttributeEnumQN, overlaid with the script's own enumerations by declareScriptTypes), so the deferral had outlived its reason.
insight: **A comment that defers a check 'until there is context' is a lead: look for the tier that now has the context before measuring from scratch.** CE0773, the code this started from, never appeared on 11.16.1 for any hand-written split (an `else` is a parse error with an explanatory hint, and the older records were the writer's own NoCase bug), so the useful result was the neighbouring gap. Measured one flow per project (a shared project hides CE0079/CE0771 behind CE1613): every value + (empty) and several values per branch clean; a value left out CE0079 on an attribute subject, a parameter subject and a nanoflow; an unknown value or the wrong case CE1613; a value in two branches CE0771 (one per branch, also when the repeat is inside a multi-value branch). An unknown value is reported alone because the build reports CE1613 first. Needs-the-project rules cannot have a `.fail.mdl` fixture: check-mdl runs `check` with no project and requires a fail fixture to fail, so MDL106's negatives live in Go tests (script enumeration, project enumeration through the fixture's Ticket.Status) plus the isolated measurements; MDL105 needs no enumeration and has the fixture. Sweep: 1,328 repo .mdl files, 0 MDL105 hits; 16 files with an enum split under `check -p`, one MDL106 hit - mdl-examples/bug-tests/1929-ended-branch-decision-one-merge.mdl, whose splits name R and G but not B; applied to a fresh project, mx check reports CE0079 for both flows, so the hit is true and the fixture (about describe round trips) was never built against the build. Control: stubbing both rules fails 11 sub-tests; `check -p` agrees with mx check on all 11 measured cases.
